{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABio76zA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhL_fZY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 403, "title": "Remove test-application allowlists from desktop voice typing; enable general native text input", "body": "## Problem

PR #402 (closed #401) merged a first desktop voice-typing implementation, but production code restricts external text input to a few applications chosen for testing. This is not the intended product behavior. **Representative test targets are not an application allowlist.** A user should be able to try dictation in their normal applications without the app refusing simply because those applications were not part of the test suite.

Affected main revision: [0d334855](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/0d3348553f867cb67cc96f931fea99f858c4bb1b).

Concrete code:
- [desktop/mac-target.m, captureTarget()](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/0d3348553f867cb67cc96f931fea99f858c4bb1b/desktop/mac-target.m#L166-L213) requires the system TextEdit or Safari bundle identifier AND installation path, rejecting all other applications before assessing the actual focused field. Additional checks restrict TextEdit to a particular document-view hierarchy and Safari to web text fields.
- [desktop/x11-accessibility.py](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/0d3348553f867cb67cc96f931fea99f858c4bb1b/desktop/x11-accessibility.py#L95-L142) requires GTK multiline views and the executable /usr/bin/mousepad via whole_edit_supported(). This is another test-target-derived production restriction.
- [docs/desktop.md](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/0d3348553f867cb67cc96f931fea99f858c4bb1b/docs/desktop.md#focused-fields) documents these restrictions as product scope.

Reproduction on macOS: focus an ordinary editable field in an application other than system TextEdit/Safari (e.g. Chrome, a code editor, a mail or chat app), then invoke the dictation shortcut. The helper rejects it by application identity, regardless of whether the field supports native text input.

## Expected outcome

**Remove artificial application restrictions from desktop voice typing.** Make the Focused Application Text Output node a general-purpose desktop text output, with ordinary native input/paste behavior.

- Remove production allowlists based on application name, bundle identifier, install path, executable path, browser brand, or toolkit merely because the application/toolkit was used for tests. Do this for macOS (primary target) and remove the analogous Mousepad-only restriction in the existing Linux X11 path. Do not replace them with larger allowlists, an opt-in list, per-app settings, or a warning/confirmation for untested applications.
- Determine the insertion method by available OS/field capabilities, not app identity. Generalize the existing selected-text and range-replacement paths where applicable, without requiring a TextEdit-specific parent hierarchy or Safari-specific document hierarchy when the same native operation is available elsewhere. Where direct editing is unavailable, consider a standard native input or clipboard/paste fallback as used by [OpenWhispr](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr) and [Handy](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy). Choose a simple practical path for ordinary editable fields, including other browsers where possible. Do not merely remove the bundle check while keeping equivalent arbitrary restrictions deeper in the code.
- Ordinary single-line inputs, multiline text fields, editable selections and application-side input constraints should work according to the target's normal native editing behavior. Do not reject an ordinary editable field solely because it might truncate, normalize, or otherwise process the supplied text. Do not require all-or-nothing edits, exact read-back or an atomic external transaction as a prerequisite for attempting ordinary text input.
- Keep normal OS authorization and the practical safeguards already agreed in #401: check the current target immediately before dispatch, stop on an observed focus/target change or cancellation, avoid duplicate dispatch and destructive clipboard handling, and do not knowingly insert into protected/password/read-only fields or submit forms. The documented residual in-flight focus race remains an accepted limitation; do not reopen that design debate. Actual missing permissions, unsupported native operations, or failed input attempts can produce an actionable error. Being untested is not an error.
- Reuse the existing host, graph/runtime and output queue. No new app-specific integrations, browser extension dependency, privileged service, UI redesign, speculative framework or exhaustive compatibility project. Prefer a small coherent fix. macOS is the priority; maintain the existing X11 implementation and remove arbitrary gates there, without requiring full browser/Wayland/OS parity.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Production target authorization and backend selection contain no test-app identity allowlists or equivalent gates. An otherwise eligible target with an arbitrary app identity is accepted; the decision depends on actual supported operations.
- [ ] Add focused deterministic regression tests demonstrating that equivalent editable targets with different application identities are treated equivalently, that ordinary single-line fields and native constraints are not categorically rejected, and that genuinely unavailable/unsafe targets are handled appropriately. Preserve applicable existing dispatch, cancel, ordering and clipboard regressions. Update obsolete tests that encoded the app-specific restrictions.
- [ ] Build the macOS app and run applicable permission-independent automated tests and focused X11 checks where available, following the repository's lightest-appropriate-layer testing policy. Existing optional permission-dependent native tests may use TextEdit/Safari/Mousepad as representative targets; there is no requirement to test every application, browser, field type or OS. Do not claim unperformed tests passed. No new permission provisioning or user/manual confirmation is a merge/closure gate.
- [ ] Update the desktop guide, error messages and PR description: distinguish examples/tested environments from actual technical limitations. Provide concise optional manual steps for trying another editor or browser, with no human approval dependency.

Do not turn this into another open-ended search for a perfect universal text-insertion API. The goal is to remove intentional restrictions and deliver practical, best-effort ordinary text input, not guarantee that every third-party application accepts every character.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Optional user testing is not a closure condition.

## Context

Follow-up to #401 and merged PR #402. The user explicitly clarified that testing two applications did not authorize restricting the product to those applications. Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md) and the existing UI/UX principles.
